subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action through `session_status`, or require a different policy boundary before any model-originated compaction can mutate active session state?
rationale: The implementation shape is narrow, but the core choice is a trust boundary: a model tool call would intentionally stop, compact, and resume active session state without an authorized sender command.

options.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
options.body: Allow a current-session-only `session_status(action: "compact")` path after the open PR is rebased and security/runtime proof is refreshed.

options.title: Require Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the direction but require an operator or tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer To Continuation Design
options.body: Do not land the narrow path until maintainers decide the broader continuation API and its security model.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
recommendation.body: Allow a current-session-only `session_status(action: "compact")` path after the open PR is rebased and security/runtime proof is refreshed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history on `session_status`, the current command/tool boundary, and adjacent session behavior.
